label: Person
name: Shuttarna III
summary:
Shuttarna III was the short-lived Mitanni king who usurped the throne in the late 14th century BC and ruled for approximately two years. His reign was marked by a series of conflicts with neighboring states, including the Hittites and the Babylonians.

Born into a life of luxury as the son of Tushratta II, Shuttarna III's ascension to the throne was likely facilitated by his father's diplomatic efforts with the Egyptians. Despite his youth and inexperience, Shuttarna III attempted to expand Mitanni's borders through military campaigns against the Hittite Empire.

However, his plans were ultimately thwarted when he was assassinated by his own brother, Tushratta III. This event sent shockwaves throughout the ancient Near East, leading to a period of instability and power struggles among the various regional kingdoms.
